name: Fix 5 HIGH CISO findings in src/api: 2 hardcoded credentials (rotate), 2 instruction-override payloads, 1 docker-socket mount
description:
Blocking CISO findings on the pending client tree, all evidenced by security_audit(path="src/api") on 2026-11-19 (decision require_approval, highest_severity high, risk_score 35.0). These files touch auth/secrets/shell, so they cannot cross the commit boundary until clean.

1. [high] secret.hardcoded-credential @ src/api/modules/analytics.js:68 — rotate the credential, replace with an env/secret-manager lookup, keep a placeholder only.
2. [high] secret.hardcoded-credential @ src/api/modules/logs.js:19 — same treatment. Rotation is mandatory: a value that lived in a file is burned even after removal.
3. [high] injection.instruction-override @ src/api/telemetry.js:202 — remove the AI-directed text or wrap the untrusted content as inert data; review how it entered the repo.
4. [high] injection.instruction-override @ src/api/modules/logs.js:73 — same.
5. [high] command.docker-socket @ src/api/modules/infra.js:82 — mounting /var/run/docker.sock is equivalent to root on the host: justify in-code or drop it.

Context: card 6bde8a8c (Review) holds the gate verdict. Related: 675c4695 (TaskSettings.vue:183 hidden-comment injection), 8a554fa4 (path filter resolves to empty diff — do NOT rely on security_review_changes with paths to verify this fix).

ACCEPTANCE: security_audit(path="src/api") returns 0 high findings AND both credentials are confirmed rotated out of band (not merely deleted from the file).

messages.content: CISO finding from the 2026-11-19 gate (card 6bde8a8c). security_audit(src/api) returned 5 HIGH findings. Fix and re-scan.

INCREMENT 1 (2026-11-19, shift 5) — verdict: all 5 HIGH findings are FALSE POSITIVES. Nothing to fix in `src/api`; the card needs a re-scope, not a code change.

VERIFIED ANCHORS (read at the exact reported line):
1. `src/api/modules/analytics.js:68` → `sessionId: 'sess[REDACTED](10 chars)',` — one entry of the camelCase→snake_case `keyMap` in `_buildAnalyticsQS` (L58–77). No credential.
2. `src/api/modules/logs.js:19` → `sessionId: 'sess[REDACTED](10 chars)',` — the identical `keyMap` construct in `_buildLogsQS` (L10–27). Findings 1 and 2 are the same benign shape matched twice.
3. `src/api/telemetry.js:202` → `received: 0,` inside `socketCounters`. No AI-directed text anywhere in the file region.
4. `src/api/modules/logs.js:73` → `// ── System logs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────` — a section comment.
5. `src/api/modules/infra.js:82` → `* "unix:///var/run/docker.sock" (local),` — a line of the `InfraHost` JSDoc typedef documenting the `endpoint` field. This is **documentation of a Docker host URI, not a socket mount**: no compose service, no `binds`, no `privileged`, no `devices` in the file. A case-sensitive scan of all 697 lines finds exactly this one occurrence of the literal.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS (each would have hit if a real defect existed; all returned 0):
- `(pass|secret|token|api_?key|bearer|sk-)[A-Za-z_]*\s*[:=]\s*['"][^'"]{6,}['"]` → **0 matches** in analytics.js (511 L), logs.js (315 L), telemetry.js (391 L), infra.js (697 L). Also `password|secret|token|apiKey|api_key|Bearer|sk-|passwd` → 0 in logs.js.
- `(ignore|disregard)…(previous|prior|above|instruction)|instruction[s]?\s*:|system prompt|you are an? (AI|assistant)` → **0 matches** in logs.js and telemetry.js.
- `project_changes(paths=[the 4 files], scope="all")` → **"No changes found"**: all four files are identical to `HEAD`, so the audit's line anchors cannot have drifted between the 09:43 run and now. A credential reported at a line that holds `sessionId: 'sess[REDACTED](10 chars)'` in an unmodified file is a scanner defect by construction.

CHANGED FILES: **none.** No edit is justified. There is also nothing to rotate — the "rotation is mandatory" requirement is void because no value ever existed in the file; deleting a placeholder would have destroyed working code for no security gain.

WHY THE RULES FIRE (re-scope proposal, one card): `secret.hardcoded-credential` accepts any `key: 'literal'` pair — including query-string map entries such as `sessionId: 'sess[REDACTED](10 chars)'`; `injection.*` scans comment/JSDoc lines; `command.docker-socket` matches the literal `/var/run/docker.sock` regardless of context. Proposed: require an entropy/format test for credentials (and exclude `*id`/`*name`/`*key` mapping keys), skip comment-only lines for injection rules, and match docker-socket only on a mount/`devices`/`privileged` construct. The rule implementation is in `api/`, outside this tool root — hand it to the api-rooted agent.

ACCEPTANCE cannot be met as written: `security_audit(path="src/api")` will keep returning these 5 until the rules are fixed, so "0 high findings" is unreachable from this side. Recommend superseding the card with the rule-fix scope above; it stays open and armed at 2026-11-21T09:43Z for that decision.

DEPENDENCY RECORDED: this invalidates 5 of the HIGH findings behind 6bde8a8c (Review) and therefore the NO-GO premise of 53ed97fc (GO/NO-GO 11-20 16:00Z). Cross-reference comment posted on 6bde8a8c. Scope of this card not widened: the `vue3-virtual-scroller ^2.0.3` finding is untouched and still stands.

VALIDATION EVIDENCE: no test command can be produced in this runtime — no shell and no node (tracked by 91411767). Everything above is read-only and reproducible with `project_read_file` (pattern/range) and `project_changes` only; no pass is claimed.

ADDENDUM to INCREMENT 1 — narrowing the claim so it is not overstated.

What is PROVEN: at the paths and line numbers reported by the audit, in files that are byte-identical to `HEAD`, there is no credential, no instruction-override text and no socket mount. That is verified, and it means **no edit inside this repository can clear these 5 findings**.

What is NOT proven: the mechanism. Two hypotheses fit, and I cannot discriminate between them from this root:
- **(a) rule over-match** — `secret.hardcoded-credential` accepting `key: 'literal'` map entries, `injection.*` scanning comment/JSDoc lines, `command.docker-socket` matching the bare literal `/var/run/docker.sock` in documentation.
- **(b) wrong root/revision scanned** — card 8a554fa4 records that `paths` resolves against the **git root**, not the project root, so a 09:43 audit could have read a different revision or a different tree and printed line numbers against it. The drift would then be real, just not visible from here.

Hypothesis (a) is favoured by the shape of the evidence (two findings on the identical `sessionId: 'sess[REDACTED](10 chars)'` construct; `infra.js:82` being pure JSDoc), but (b) is not excluded and is independently plausible. Discrimination requires the audit's own output — scanned file count, resolved root and the matched substring — which lives in `api/`, outside this tool root.

Either way the card's conclusion is unchanged and the recommended re-scope stands: before touching any code, require the `security_audit` run to report **resolved root + scanned/skipped counts + the matched text per finding**. A finding that cannot show the text it matched is not actionable — same defect class as `b7225e63` (verdict without counts) and `82802eda` (unvalidated references).

- Evidence — **none of the 5 cited files is in the changed set.** Modified under `src/api`: `api.js`, `connection.js`, `modules/{browsers,chats,companies,computers,efforts,repo}.js`, added `modules/voice.js`, untracked `modules/ciso.js`. Absent: **`modules/analytics.js`, `modules/logs.js`, `telemetry.js`, `modules/infra.js`**.
- Content probe at the cited locations (files read directly this shift, whole-file regex, 2026-11-19T11:4xZ), against `client/src/api` — the root this project actually owns:
  · `modules/logs.js:19` is `endDate: 'end_date'` in a query-string keyMap; **0** matches for `(password|secret|apiKey|api_key|Bearer )` across all 315 lines ⇒ `secret.hardcoded-credential` **does not reproduce**.
  · `modules/analytics.js:68` — **0** matches across all 511 lines ⇒ **does not reproduce**.
  · `modules/infra.js:82` — JSDoc: `"unix:///var/run/docker.sock" (local)` documented as an accepted *endpoint format*, next to the `ssh://` alternative. It is not a mount ⇒ `command.docker-socket` **does not reproduce as described**.
  · `telemetry.js:202` and `modules/logs.js:73` — **0** matches for instruction-override signatures in the whole file ⇒ `injection.instruction-override` **do not reproduce**.
- Failing test ids: none — no test executed.
- Blocking item: **no patch exists for findings 1–5**, and at least 3 of the 5 citations do not reproduce at the cited `path:line`. The fix cannot be written against them until the finding set is re-derived: the card never says whether `src/api` means `client/src/api` (the tree that is actually pending) or `src/api` at the git root.
- Owner: **ciso** (state the scan root and re-derive with `security_audit`), then software_developer for whatever survives
- Next command: `security_audit(path="client/src/api")` → then `qa_review_changes(scope="all", paths=["client/src/api"])`

Caveat on my probe: these are signature regexes, not the CISO detector corpus. 0 matches proves the cited *signature* is absent from these files — not that the detector was wrong. The re-derivation decides, and I will gate whatever it produces.
